Subject: Private fleet patching window — request and constraints

Hi Olga,

We need to plan the maintenance window for the private deployment in our VPC (cluster-id: acme-prod-01). Compliance has flagged the OS and runtime CVEs and wants a coordinated patch between Oct 20-22. Can Redwood do a staggered patch with a pinned-version eviction approach instead of a full fleet reboot? Key constraints:
- 1-hour max downtime per service (target)
- No more than 10% concurrent node cordons in the primary region
- We need an explicit canary/prod staging cadence (canary -> small cohort -> full rollout)

Please propose a plan that includes:
- How you’ll handle version pin eviction without rolling back client API contracts
- Network cordon/uncordon steps and circuit-breaker settings
- A rollback trigger matrix tied to error thresholds and latency regressions

Thanks,
Marco
Platform Reliability — Acme Financial

Hi Marco — thanks for the heads up.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Maintenance window: Oct 21 00:00 - Oct 21 08:00 UTC (we'll stage canaries starting Oct 21 00:00 UTC)
- Approach: pinned-version eviction (pin -> stage -> evict) with explicit KV cache warmup steps to avoid cold-start latency spikes
- Cordon policy: max cordon concurrency = 8% of cluster nodes; threshold override only by SRE on-call
- Canary cadence: 2 canary nodes (10 minutes observation), then 15% cohort (30 minutes), then rolling remainder (5m per node drain with 2m verification)
- Rollback triggers: error-rate + latency combined rule (>=3x baseline error-rate for 5m OR p99 latency +40% for 10m)

Attachments attached: patch-runbook-v2.pdf (detailed runbook), cordon-checklist.md (operator steps). I also included a short simulation log from our local KV eviction dry run (kv-eviction-sim.log).

Operational notes:
- We'll perform a pre-flight health snapshot and maintain continuous tracing and token-level cost sampling so you can correlate traffic patterns to tail latency.
- We will avoid simultaneous control-plane upgrades; only data-plane runtime patches are planned.

Next actions:
1) Confirm the Oct 21 window is acceptable to Acme compliance and ops.
2) Approve the canary cadence and escalation contacts (I included SRE: jonas.weber and Platform Eng: dev.patel).

I'll loop Jonas with technical details next.

— Olga

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marco.ruiz@acme-financial.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 20:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private fleet patching window — pin eviction mechanics and network cordon details

TL;DR: pin eviction will be implemented as an explicit two-phase state change (PIN->DRAINABLE->EVICT) to give control-plane and clients time to adapt.

Technical details:
- Step 0 (preflight): collect KV usage heatmap, open file descriptors, and active KV sessions; snapshot in snapshot-YYYYMMDD.json (internal).
- Step 1 (PIN->DRAINABLE): mark nodes as drainable in the control plane; KV cache remains readable but write-paths increment a "drain-intent" header so clients can gracefully re-open sessions to other nodes.
- Step 2 (live warmup): create ephemeral warmup pods on target nodes to pre-populate KV prefixes most used in last 24h. This avoids p99 spikes.
- Step 3 (EVICT): once warmup is validated and load balancing redistributed, remove pin and evict.

Network cordon/uncordon steps (operator CLI):
1) cordon <node-id> --reason=patch --until=2026-10-21T01:30Z
2) drain <node-id> --grace-period=300s --force-evict-active-sessions
3) run integration smoke test (~90s) against canary endpoint (smoke-canary.acme.internal)
4) uncordon if smoke fails or proceed to patch if smoke passes

Automation notes: we will run canary verification probes via the Redwood console and expose a short-lived read-only dashboard to Acme ops. If the rollback matrix triggers, the orchestrator halts the rollout and re-pins the affected cohort. Manual rollback requires SRE approval.

Operational safeguard: we’ll enforce a soft circuit breaker at the edge that will route 50% of retries to a standby model variant if p95 tail latency exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive windows.

I'll attach a small snippet of the cordon-checklist to the runbook.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
